f: Reapers are proficient with simple weapons, as well as light armor and bucklers. In addition, if this is this character's first level in any class, they may select a martial tradition of their choice.

A reaper may combine spheres and talents to create magical effects. A reaper is considered a Low-Caster. They may use their choice of Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma as their casting ability modifier and must make this choice at 1st level. (Note: all casters may select a casting tradition the first time they gain the casting class feature.)

A reaper gains a small reservoir of energy they can call on to create truly wondrous effects, called a spell pool. This pool contains a number of spell points equal to their level + their casting ability modifier (minimum: 1). This pool replenishes once per day after roughly 8 hours of rest.

A reaper gains combat or magic talents according to Table: Reaper, gaining their choice of combat or magic talents at each level they would gain a talent. Reapers use their casting ability modifier as their practitioner modifier.

At 1st level, a reaper gains the Duelist sphere as a bonus talent, or a talent from the Duelist sphere if they already possess the base sphere. Additionally, the reaper gains the Bloody Slasher drawback, but gains the Ooze Ichor talent instead of Long Cuts.

At 1st level, a reaper selects a creature type from the ranger favored enemies table. They gain a +2 bonus on Bluff, Knowledge, Perception, Sense Motive, and Survival checks against creatures of their selected type. Likewise, the reaper gets a +2 bonus on weapon attack and damage rolls against them. A reaper may make Knowledge skill checks untrained when attempting to identify these creatures.

At 5th level and every 5 levels thereafter (10th, 15th, and 20th level), this bonus increases by +2. Unlike a ranger, the reaper does not select an additional creature type at these levels. Instead, they may change their favored prey by meditating on a reaper trophy they've created for 1 minute. The trophy does not need to be held, only carried on the reaper's body.

The reaper may create a small object called a reaper trophy with the remains of a creature they've slain in battle and 1 hour of work. Whenever a reaper meditates on a reaper trophy they've created, their favored prey type changes to the type corresponding to the creature used to make the trophy.

At 1st level, a reaper must select a cult to focus on. A cult is an area of intense occult study centred around a specific creature, and the root of their eldritch powers. The reaper learns how to hunt the creatures belonging to the creature's type, and eventually gains those creatures' powers. At 1st, 5th, and every 4 levels after, the reaper gains an ability specific to that cult.

**Cult of the Blight [Baron’s Otherworldly Citadel]**

In your battle against contaminating forces which seem to subsume the world in their mindless hunger, you straddle the line between a reasoning being and an unthinking plague. In forsaking the constituency that oozes and plants feed upon, you hope to starve our or even consume such threats yourself.
At 1st level, you are always treated as if you've selected plants and oozes with your favored prey class feature, in addition to the currently selected creature type.

At 5th level, you can extract a servitor from your body to carry out your will. As a standard action, you can have your servitor detach itself from your body as a separate creature with the statistics of a plant companion with an effective druid level of your reaper level (the type of plant companion is chosen when you gain this ability). The servitor can reattach itself to you as a standard action. When attached to you, the servitor has fast healing equal to your reaper level. If a servitor dies, it can be replaced in the same manner as a normal plant companion.
If you die, your servitor gradually becomes you, replacing its own statistics with yours after 1d6 days. When this process is complete, you take full control of the servitor as if it was your original character.
While your servitor is separated from your body, it carries a fragment of its consciousness with it, imposing a -2 penalty on Will saves as well as Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma-based skill checks on you.

At 9th level, your body takes on an amorphous form as ooze overtakes it. You gain the compression universal monster ability and no longer need to breathe. You and your servitor do not take any damage or take any penalty from diseases. You can still contract diseases and spread them to others, but you are otherwise immune to their effects.
Your mutable physiology is also unwieldy and difficult to control. You take a -2 penalty on initiative checks

At 13th level, your essence contaminates your environment and bends it to your will. You may ignore the immunity of plants and oozes to mind-affecting effects (even if they are normally mindless). Whenever you affect a mindless ooze or plant in this way, you gain enough influence over the creature for it to carry out simple commands (such as “guard this room,” “flank this foe,” or “bring me that dead body”). Any hostile creature which detects you with blindsense or blindsight becomes sickened for as long as it does so.
As your contagion spreads, you become a living biohazard to your allies. Any of your allies within 30 feet of you (excluding yourself and and your servitor) suffer a -2 penalty to all saving throws. You may spend a spell point as a free action to suppress this penalty for 1 minute.

At 17th level, your identity becomes entwined with a potent disease known as living plague. Your touch and natural attacks as well as the touch and natural attacks of your servitor carry the living plague disease. You automatically know how many creatures are infected with living plague and can detect them as per lifesense out to a range of 1 mile. Additionally, you can perceive using any infected individual’s senses as per the Shared Perception talent from the Divination Sphere and communicate with them telepathically. You may take these actions even if you are dead.
In addition, if both you and your servitor are dead, any instance of the living plague gradually reforms into you. If a creature dies while carrying your living plague while you are dead, you reclaim the creature's body and return in its location as per the Greater Resurrection talent from the Life Sphere.
As you are a manifest disease, healing you proves immensely difficult. The number of hit points you recover from any source are reduced by half (minimum 0). You may spend a spell point as an immediate action to ignore this healing reduction for 1 round.

**Living Plague**
**Type** disease, contact or injury; Save Fortitude DC 10 + ½ your reaper level + your casting ability modifier
**Onset** 1 day; **Frequency** 1/day
**Effect** 2d4 damage to an ability score of your choice, chosen each time the creature fails its saving throw; **Cure** 2 consecutive saves

At 20th level, if you surrender your soul, you gain the ooze creature template, save that your alignment is not affected and your ability scores are not reduced. You do not gain or lose any sense from gaining the ooze creature type.
At 1st level, the reaper is always treated as if they have selected magical beast with their favored prey class feature, in addition to the currently selected creature type.

At 5th level, the reaper’s body begins to subtly become more monstrous, growing scales, chitinous plates, or dense matted fur. The reaper’s base natural armor increases by +2 and stacks with any other natural armor they possess. Whenever they are struck by a cold iron weapon, or they touch an object made of cold iron, their body quivers uncontrollably, taking a -2 penalty on attack rolls for 1 round. The reaper retains the effects of this ability even while under the effects of a polymorph effect (or other effect that would suppress abilities reliant on the target’s natural form).
Claws that Bite, Jaws that Catch (Su)

At 9th level, the reaper’s body manifests hideous and monstrous appendages.

The reaper chooses of two of the following:

- 1 arm, as the extra arm trait from the Alteration sphere Additional Limbs talent.
- 1 bite (primary, 1d6 Medium, 1d4 Small) plus grab.
- 2 claws (primary, 1d6 Medium, 1d4 Small) plus 1d6 bleed.
- 1 gore (primary, 1d6 Medium, 1d4 Small) plus push.
- 1 prehensile tail with a stinger (primary, 1d4 Medium, 1d3 Small) plus poison (stinger – injury; save Fort DC 10 + 1/2 their reaper level + their casting ability modifier; frequency 1/round for 4 rounds; effect 1d2 Con damage; cure 2 saves).
- 2 tentacles (secondary, 1d4 Medium, 1d3 Small). These tentacles cannot be used to wield weapons or shields. However, the tentacles are agile and dexterous, and may be used as normal limbs and hands for any other purpose.

The reaper must have appropriate limbs or appendages when choosing these natural attacks (see the Alteration sphere for similar natural attack requirements, such as gaining claws requiring arms or front legs) and cannot select a choice more than once. The additional appendages and natural attacks from this ability have an ethereal, sickly glow to them, and are noticeably unnatural. The reaper may spend 1 spell point as a standard action to reselect their choices from this ability, or to suppress or enable the natural attacks from this ability. If the reaper suppresses this ability, their animalistic nature takes a toll on their mental capacity, causing them to act more feral and suffer a -4 penalty on all Intelligence-based skill checks and ability checks as long as this ability is suppressed.

In addition, whenever the reaper performs an attack action, they may make an additional attack with a natural attack granted by this ability at a -5 penalty as a free action.

At 13th level, the reaper may spend a spell point as a swift action to temporarily tap into a primal rage. For the next minute, the reaper’s size increases to the next category larger, they gain a +4 size bonus to Strength and Constitution and the natural armor bonus from the chimeric adaptations ability increases by 2. The reaper’s size modifier for AC and attacks changes as appropriate to their new size category. This ability does not change the reaper’s speed. Determine the reaper’s space and reach as appropriate to their new size. Overwhelming might is a not a polymorph effect, but it does not stack with other size changes, such as the Alteration sphere Size Change talent.

When the reaper uses overwhelming might, they become ravenous and irrational. If they did not damage a creature during their previous turn, the reaper takes 1d6 points of nonlethal damage and is sickened for 1 round. If the reaper is immune to nonlethal damage, the damage dealt is lethal instead. This sickened condition bypasses any immunity to the sickened condition the reaper may possess.

At 17th level, the reaper takes on the mantle of the king of monsters. The reaper gains DR 5/–, which stacks with all other sources of DR /–, and immunity to bleed, death effects, disease, fire and poison.

In addition, once per round during their turn, the reaper may spend a spell point as a free action to attempt a new saving throw against one adverse condition they are suffering from that normally grants a saving throw, using the effect’s original DC. If the reaper is affected by multiple adverse conditions, they choose one adverse condition to attempt a new saving throw versus. The reaper may use this ability even if they are normally unable to take actions due to an adverse condition.

This beastly boon comes with a price, an innate demand for perfection. Whenever the reaper first fails a saving throw against a non-harmless effect that causes an adverse condition, they take 3d6 points of nonlethal damage which bypasses any damage reduction they possess and cannot be prevented. If the reaper is immune to nonlethal damage, the damage dealt is lethal instead.

**Note:** For the purposes of this ability, an “adverse condition” is a condition, such as entangled, shaken, or paralyzed, caused by an effect with a saving throw. This ability does not work on conditions caused by effects without a saving throw, such as becoming shaken by the Intimidate skill.

At 20th level, if the reaper surrenders their soul, they gain the animal lord template (Pathfinder Roleplaying Game Bestiary 3 pg. 14), and choose a species affinity of their choice, unless they would be unable to gain it due to their creature type. In addition, the reaper is treated as a magical beast for the purposes of effects targeting creatures by type (such as a ranger’s favored enemy and bane weapons, but not for prerequisites).
At 1st level, you are always treated as if you've selected undead with your favored prey class feature, in addition to the currently selected creature type.

At 5th level, you learn to temporarily sustain your energy with the blood you spill on the battlefield. Whenever you inflict bleed onto a creature, you gain an amount of temporary hit points equal to your practitioner modifier. These temporary hit points stack with each other, but you cannot gain temporary hit points from inflicting bleed damage on a creature who is already bleeding, even if this bleed damage would be greater than what they are currently suffering. Temporary hit points from this ability expire after 1 minute.

Whenever you lose all the temporary hit points gained from blood thirst within 1 round, your lust for blood weakens your resolve and you take a -2 penalty to AC for 1 minute or until you gain temporary hit points with blood thirst, whichever comes first.

At 9th level, you can shed your corporeal form by channeling your essence into pure blood. You can spend 1 spell point as a standard action to gain the effects of a gaseous form spell, treating your class level as your caster level for the effects of this ability. In addition, whenever a creature attempts to attack you with a melee attack while in this form, they must succeed on a Fortitude save (DC = 10 + 1/2 your HD + your practitioner modifier) or suffer bleed damage equal to your practitioner modifier. This bleed damage is affected by abilities such as bloodletter and blood thirst as normal.

While using crimson cloud, your thoughts succumb to an obsession over blood and your mind becomes susceptible to mental attacks as you take a -2 penalty to Perception checks and Will saves until you return to your normal form.

At 13th level, you can spend 1 spell point as a standard action to gain a gaze attack as per the universal monster rules for 1 minute with the following effect: All creatures who meet your gaze must succeed on a Will save (DC = 10 + 1/2 your HD + your practitioner modifier) or are charmed as per charm monster, using your class level as your caster level for the purpose of this effect and its duration.

Channeling your soul in order to charm others causes violent disdain for others in your mind, and you must feed in order to make others a part of you. When you use vampiric charm, you become sickened until you inflict bleed damage onto another creature.

At 17th level, you gain damage reduction 10/magic and silver as your flesh becomes tough and numb with necrotic energy. Additionally, whenever another creature attempts to attack you with a melee weapon, they must succeed on a Fortitude save (DC = 10 + 1/2 your HD + your practitioner modifier) or take 2d6 points of negative energy damage. Creatures that would be healed by negative energy succeed on this save automatically.

This deadening of your flesh comes at a price, and you become sensitive to sunlight. Whenever you are in direct sunlight, you are fatigued and take 1 point of damage per round. The fatigue ends as soon as you find cover from the sun. You may spend 1 spell point to suppress this weakness to sunlight for 1 minute per reaper level.

At 20th level, if you surrender your soul, you gain the vampire template unless you would be unable to gain it due to your creature type. Your type changes to undead (augmented), gaining all benefits of the template. Due to your type of transformation, you do not gain the template's weakness to sunlight, although you do gain all its other weaknesses.
At 1st level, you are always treated as if you've selected aberrations with your favored prey class feature, in addition to the currently selected creature type.
Cult of the Great Old Ones

At 5th level, you may temporarily project your mind beyond the normal limits of geometry, effectively summoning a tendril of psychic energy as a swift action by spending 1 spell point. Once summoned, the tendril attacks a random enemy within 10 feet of you once each turn on your initiative, using your base attack bonus + your practitioner modifier to perform a melee touch attack and dealing 1d6 + your reaper level in nonlethal damage on a successful hit.

After 1 minute, the tendril dissipates and you suffer 1d6 points of nonlethal damage as your conscious mind recoils from its abuse. If you are immune to nonlethal damage, the damage dealt is lethal instead.
Cult of the Great Old Ones

At 9th level, whenever you suffer a critical hit, you may spend 1 spell point as an immediate action to contort spacial reality around the attack and turn it into a normal hit. Whenever you use mutable form, you are sickened until the end of your next turn as conflicting messages from your nerves overwhelm you. If you are already sickened, the durations overlap (they do not stack).
Cult of the Great Old Ones

At 13th level, you may spend 1 spell point as a move action to distort space within 30 feet radius around you as greater realities begin to merge with your own. Every creature except yourself treats this area around you as difficult terrain, even if using nonstandard movement forms such as flight. Additionally, all enemies must succeed on a Will save (DC = 10 + 1/2 your HD + your practitioner modifier) or suffer 1d4 points of nonlethal damage per two reaper levels you possess the first time they enter the area.

After 1 minute, the area around you returns to normal and you suffer 3d6 points of nonlethal damage as your mental faculties fail to resist the spatial contortions. If you are immune to nonlethal damage, the damage dealt is lethal instead.
Cult of the Great Old Ones

At 17th level, you may spend 2 spell points as a standard action and utter a single word of horrific, eldritch truth. This word can be repeated by none but understood by all. Every other creature within a 100 foot radius of your location who hears the word suffers 10d6 points of nonlethal damage and must succeed on a Will save (DC = 10 + 1/2 your HD + your practitioner modifier) or become dazed for 1 round and confused and deafened for 1 minute per reaper level you possess. Any creatures unable of hearing you speak (including those using earplugs or the like) are immune to forbidden utterance.

Whenever you use forbidden utterance, you become deafened for 1 minute and dazed for 1 round. Even the speaker of such a horrible revelation cannot resist its dreadful clarity.
Cult of the Great Old Ones
At 20th level, if you surrender your soul, you gain the half-aberration template (below). Your type changes to aberration, gaining all abilities of the template.
Cult of the Great Old Ones

At 1st level, you are always treated as if you've selected creatures with the incorporeal subtype with your favored prey class feature, in addition to the currently selected creature type. In addition, you may apply your favored prey bonus to any skill checks made against haunts.

At 5th level, you gain the haunt channeler class feature of a medium, using your reaper level as your effective medium level. Whenever you attempt a saving throw against the effects of a channeled haunt, you may spend a spell point to add your favored enemy bonus to the saving throw.

In addition, you may spend a spell point to see any objects or beings that are invisible within your range of vision, as well as any that are ethereal, as if they were normally visible for a number of minutes equal to your reaper level. Such creatures are visible to you as translucent shapes, allowing you easily to discern the difference between visible, invisible, and ethereal creatures. While this effect is active, your maximum vision range is reduced to 60 feet.

At 9th level, any weapons you are wielding or armor you are wearing gains the ghost touch special ability. In addition, if you reduce an incorporeal creature to 0 hit points or fewer, you can instead leave the creature at 1 hit point and consume the creature as an immediate action. A consumed creature is contained in your body and grants you a +1 bonus on either attack rolls, saving throws, or skill checks, chosen by the spirit eater, and a number of temporary hit points equal to the consumed creature’s Hit Dice. These bonuses stack with themselves and last for 24 hours after you consume a spirit or until the spirit is released (whichever comes first). You cannot gain these benefits from consuming a spirit you have consumed before.

Your body can hold a number of creatures equal to half your favored prey bonus. If you attempt to consume another creature after this point, you must release another consumed creature of your choice. You can release a consumed creature as a free action. A consumed creature attempts to escape after 24 hours. You can attempt to keep a consumed creature in your body by attempting a Will save (DC = 10 + half your level + twice the number of the creatures you have contained in your body). If you succeed, the consumed creatures remain, but they impose a -4 penalty to saving throws against possession and mind-affecting effects. A released creature is destroyed as if it were reduced to 0 hit points and can reconstitute again later, if able. You may spend two spell points for each creature you have contained in your body to automatically succeed at this saving throw.

At 13th level, you gain the wraith form ability of a wraith of your reaper level. In addition, you may select wraith haunts in place of reaper talents, using your reaper level as your effective wraith level.
Stepping directly into the incorporeal realm is taxing. Whenever you return from your wraith form to your corporeal form, you become fatigued for a number of rounds equal to 2 times the number of rounds spent in wraith form. You cannot enter a wraith form while fatigued or exhausted but may spend a spell point to negate this fatigue.

At 17th level, you gain the possession and greater possession abilities of a wraith of your reaper level. However, your own sense of self becomes foreign to you as you explore these other forms. Whenever you stop possessing a creature and return to your original body, you suffer 4 points of ability burn to a random ability score unless you spend a spell point.

At 20th level, if you surrender your soul, you gain either the ghost or prana ghost template unless you would be unable to gain it due to your creature type. For the purpose of ghost abilities, treat your character level as your CR. Due to your type of transformation, you do not gain the rejuvenation ability. Any instances of the extra wraith form and lingering incorporeality wraith haunts may immediately be retrained for other wraith haunts for which you qualify.
You make take on a corporeal form or return to your incorporeal state as a move action. While corporeal, you lose the incorporeal ability and gain a Strength score equal to your Strength score from before you gained this ability.

At 1st level, choose either air, earth, fire, or water. you are always treated as if you've selected outsiders with the chosen subtype with your favored prey class feature, in addition to the currently selected creature type. You can spend 8 hours of meditation to change the selected subtype to another one of the four options. At GM discretion, you may also select other subtypes of outsider not listed as ranger favored enemies such as aether, wood, metal, or elemental.

At 5th level, you may spend a spell point as a swift action to grant any weapon you are holding a +1 enhancement bonus for 1 minute. For every four levels beyond 1st, the weapon gains another +1 enhancement bonus, to a maximum of +5 at 17th level. These bonuses can be added to the weapon, stacking with existing weapon enhancement to a maximum of +5. Multiple uses of this ability do not stack with themselves. These bonuses can be used to add any of the following weapon properties: corrosive, corrosive burst, flaming, flaming burst, frost, icy burst, shock, shocking burst, or thundering.
Your essence becomes volatile as you channel this power, rendering you vulnerable. While this ability is active, you take a -2 penalty to AC. You may spend a spell point as a free action to suppress this penalty for 1 minute.

At 9th level, you are able to insulate yourself against the dangers of the elemental planes. You are considered to be constantly under the effects of the Breathless and Planar Refuge aegis talents from the Protection Sphere and gain resistance to one of acid, cold, electricity, or fire equal to 1/2 your class level + your practitioner modifier (you can spend 8 hours of meditation to change this energy type).
As you connect yourself further to the Inner Planes, you take on the more extreme weaknesses of elemental beings. While you have energy resistance selected, you also gain vulnerability to another type (fire if you have cold and vice versa, acid if you have electricity and vice versa). You may spend a spell point as a free action to suppress this vulnerability for 1 minute.

At 13th, you can transform yourself into a hulking mass of primal elements by spending a spell point as a standard action. For a number of rounds equal to your casting ability modifier, your size increases to either Large or Huge, you take a -2 penalty to Dexterity, and in place of any normal size modifiers to ability scores you gain a +12 size bonus to your Strength, Dexterity, and Constitution scores which can be divided between them in any way you wish (to a maximum of +8 in any one score). While in this form, your natural armor bonus increases by +4. You are also immune to bleed damage, critical hits, and sneak attacks while in titan form and gain DR/— equal to half your reaper level.
As you return to your original form, the stability of all four elements in your mortal form becomes limiting. You become staggered for 1 minute.

At 17th level, you delve into the elemental planes’ deepest secrets, emerging with the power to rearrange the building blocks of the multiverse. Your abilities ignore any energy resistance or hardness that targets may possess and all of your attacks count as silver, cold iron, and adamantine for the purpose of bypassing damage reduction. Your energy resistance from Planar Voyager changes to immunity to the chosen damage type.
This connection to the elemental planes leaves your consciousness vulnerable to control or assault. You take a -3 penalty to Will saves. You may spend a spell point as a free action to suppress this penalty for 1 minute.

At 20th level, if you surrender your soul, you gain the elemental-infused template unless you would be unable to gain it due to your creature type. You do not take a penalty to an ability score from gaining this template. You can spend 8 hours in meditation to change the options selected with the elemental-infused template.
At 1st level, you are always treated as if you've selected fey with your favored prey class feature, in addition to the currently selected creature type.

At 5th level, you may grow or retract an elongated black beak as a swift action, giving you a bite attack as a primary natural weapon which deals 1d8 damage (1d6 for a small reaper) plus your Strength modifier on a successful hit. Additionally, whenever you successfully hit a creature with your bite attack, the creature suffers bleed damage equal to half your reaper level.

The influence of vilderavn magic within you causes you to feel a sharp aversion to cold iron. You suffer a -2 penalty to attack rolls against creatures holding objects made of cold iron, and weapons made of cold iron deal additional damage to you on successful hits equal to half your Hit Dice.

At 9th level, you may project or retract a fey aura which sows disloyalty, doubt, and dissension in your victims. While the aura is active, hostile creatures within 30 feet of you that fail a Will saving throw (DC = 10 + 1/2 your HD + your practitioner modifier) are shaken and no longer treated as allies to other creatures, becoming unable to provide flanking, use or benefit from teamwork feats or aid another actions, or allow other creatures to move through their space as long as they remain within your aura and for 1d4 rounds afterwards.

Any spell or effect that requires a willing target fails if used on an affected creature, and even harmless effects require an attack roll (if applicable) and require affected creatures to attempt a saving throw to resist their effects (if a save is allowed). This is a mind-affecting fear effect.

The paranoia and suspicion you are able to sow gradually seeps into your soul, dampening your emotions. You must always attempt to make saving throws against effects with morale bonuses, and you suffer a -2 penalty to attack rolls, skill checks, and saving throws while affected by any morale bonus.

At 13th level, you may spend 1 spell point as an immediate action to target an enemy within 30 feet, bringing misfortune and doom upon them. The target must succeed on a Will saving throw (DC = 10 + 1/2 your HD + your practitioner modifier) or suffer a penalty to attack rolls made against you equal to your practitioner modifier for 1 minute. If the target is slain while under this effect, you gain access to that creature’s memories from the last week.

You can spend 1 spell point as a standard action to assume or dismiss a perfect likeness of a creature slain by this ability at any time as if using the Alteration sphere Perfect Disguise talent, gaining a +10 bonus on Bluff and Disguise checks made to impersonate it.

Stealing the memories and faces of others causes you to struggle with bouts of depersonalization, making it more difficult to coordinate with allies. The first time in a given round when you would be considered an ally to another creature (such as for a spell effect, teamwork feat, or providing flanking bonuses), you must succeed at a Will saving throw (DC = 10 + 1/2 your HD + your practitioner modifier) or suffer the effects of your Shatter Loyalties aura until the beginning of your next turn.

At 17th level, your bite attack granted by Blood Beak threatens a critical hit on an 18–20 and gains the deadly special weapon feature. If a vilderavn kills a humanoid or fey foe with a hit from its bite attack (including a coup de grace), it can tear out the victim’s heart and consume its soul. Creatures that witness this brutality are frightened for 1d4 rounds, or shaken for 1 round if they succeed at a Will save (DC = 10 + 1/2 your HD + your practitioner modifier). Also, you gain the benefits of the Death sphere Necrotic Feeding talent, using your reaper level as your base caster level, and anyone attempting to revive the creature must succeed at an MSB roll or fail.

The vitality you gain from eating the hearts of your prey satisfies you so intensely that it becomes difficult to live without. If you go at least 24 hours without using your Heart Eater ability, you suffer a -2 penalty to Charisma-based skill checks, and a -2 penalty to attack rolls made against creatures that aren't bleeding while you perceive a bleeding creature. Killing a creature with Heart Eater removes this penalty. This penalty is an (emotion) effect.

At 20th level, if you surrender your soul, you gain the fey creature template unless you would be unable to gain it due to your creature type. Your type changes to fey (augmented), gaining all benefits of the template. All changes and abilities from this template are corvid-themed as you are corrupted into a twisted form of vilderavn.
At 1st level, you are always treated as if you've selected outsiders with the evil subtype with your favored prey class feature, in addition to the currently selected creature type.

At 5th level, your tongue darkens as you gain the ability to speak directly to the souls of others. As a standard action, you may spend 1 spell point to establish a telepathic link with a creature up to 100 feet away from you within line of sight and effect. An unwilling creature can resist the telepathic link by succeeding on a Will saving throw (DC = 10 + 1/2 your HD + your practitioner modifier). For 1 minute per reaper level, you are able to communicate with that creature as the telepathy universal monster ability and perceive the creature as if you had blindsense while within 100 feet of the target. A creature may attempt a Will save against this link once every minute it is active, breaking the link on a successful save. At 11th level, you may use this ability as a swift action.

Learning to communicate via thoughts leaves you less finesse when communicating normally, imposing a -4 penalty on Bluff, Diplomacy, and Intimidate checks when not communicating through telepathy.

At 9th level, your ability to link with the souls of others deepens. You may spend 1 spell point as part of an attack action to mark your target with a symbol-shaped scar of your power. If the attack hits, in addition to the normal effects, the creature must succeed on a Fortitude save (DC = 10 + 1/2 your HD + your practitioner modifier). On a failed save, the wound or area of contact scars over, imposing a -2 penalty to AC against your attacks and a -2 penalty to Will saves against your abilities. While the creature retains this mark, you can use your Blackened Tongue ability on the creature and communicate with it as long as you are within 1 mile of the creature, ignoring line of sight or effect. This mark is a (curse) effect and can only be removed by use of the Life sphere Break Enchantment talent or a similar effect.

Abusing fiendish techniques to erode the souls of others causes disturbances in your body, forcing you to succeed on a Fortitude saving throw or become sickened for 1 minute whenever you touch or are damaged by a good-aligned object or weapon.

At 13th level, you learn how to use the fiendish corruption growing inside you to act as a breach for the underworld. You may spend 1 spell point as a move action to spew forth fire and ash in a 30-foot radius emanation around you which lasts a number of rounds equal to your practitioner modifier before dispersing naturally. This smoke affects creatures as if using the Nature sphere Fog Mastery talent to produce a smokescreen, with a save DC of 10 + 1/2 your HD + your practitioner modifier. Creatures who fail their Fortitude saves also take 1d6 points of fire damage per 2 levels of reaper you possess, changing to profane damage if they are affected by Nether Brand. You are immune to the effects of this burning smoke, though it still obscures your vision as normal.

Using your soul as a bridge between yourself and the lower planes leaves you more susceptible to the tactics of otherworldly fiends. You suffer a -2 penalty to saves against all mind-affecting effects, which increases to -4 when the user is an outsider with the evil subtype.

At 17th level, you gain the ability to eviscerate the souls of your enemies, tapping into your heart's hunger for the souls of the living. You may spend 1 spell point as part of an attack action against a living creature. If the attack hits, the creature must succeed on a Fortitude save (DC = 10 + 1/2 your HD + your practitioner modifier). On a failed save, they take profane damage equal to one-quarter of their current hit points and you gain temporary hit points equal to your reaper level that last for 1 minute. If the creature was affected by Nether Brand, the damage does not naturally heal and can only be magically healed by succeeding on an MSB check while the Nether Brand remains.
Relying on siphoning the souls of others to sustain your own corrupted soul weakens your body's ability to heal damage. You only heal half the damage you normally would from effects that would increase your hit points.

At 20th level, if you surrender your soul, you gain the half fiend template unless you would be unable to gain it due to your creature type. Your type changes to outsider (evil, native), gaining all benefits of the template. You may choose to gain an alternate half-fiend template as long as it does not increase the CR of the template.
At 1st level, you are always treated as if you've selected humanoids with the shapechanger subtype with your favored prey class feature, in addition to the currently selected creature type.

At 5th level, your flesh grows tough yet mutable, and you gain damage reduction 5/magic and silver. Whenever you are stuck by a magic silver weapon or you touch magical silver, your skin burns as you take a -2 penalty to AC and lose the benefit of your damage reduction for 1 minute.

At 9th level, your jaw elongates and your teeth grow long and sharp, giving you a bite primary natural weapon which deals 1d8 damage (1d6 for a small reaper) plus your Strength modifier on a successful hit. Additionally, whenever you successfully hit a creature with your bite attack, you may attempt a trip against the target as a free action.

Whenever you successfully deal damage with a bite attack, lycanthropic hunger surges through your body and you gain a -2 penalty to attack anybody you haven't already bitten for 1 minute. Successfully dealing damage with a bite attack to a creature while suffering from this penalty switches the target of the hunger to that new creature.

If you already had a bite attack, it is replaced with this one as the wolf asserts its influence over your body.

At 13th level, you can spend 1 spell point as a move action to let out a terrifying, unnatural howl. All enemies within 30 feet of you must succeed on a Will save (DC = 10 + 1/2 your HD + your practitioner modifier) or become panicked for a number of rounds equal to your practitioner modifier on a failed save. On a successful save, they are instead shaken for 1 round.

Whenever you use rending howl, you must feed on the resultant fear you've instilled in your enemies. For 1 minute, if you attack a target who isn't suffering from a fear effect, you become fatigued.

At 17th level, you can spend 2 spell points as an immediate action to break loose of any bonds with the power of the wolf. Until the end of your turn, you gain the benefit of a freedom of movement spell treating your class level as your caster level for the effects of this ability and become immune to the following status conditions: blinded, confused, cowering, dazed, deafened, entangled, exhausted, fascinated, fatigued, frightened, nauseated, panicked, paralyzed, petrified, shaken, sickened, staggered, and stunned. At the end of your turn, if you are still the subject of an ongoing effect that would cause any of these status conditions, you suffer the conditions as normal.

When you use wolf heart surge, your soul is overwhelmed by the urge to hunt. For the next minute, if you spend a turn without attempting to harm another creature, you become exhausted for 1 minute.

At 20th level, if you surrender your soul, you gain the lycanthrope template unless you would be unable to gain it due to your creature type, treating yourself as a natural lycanthrope mixed with a dire wolf. You gain the shapechanger subtype, gaining all the benefits of the template except that the damage reduction you gain is damage reduction 10/magic and silver and your bite attack in all forms is the bite attack granted by your primal hunger ability.
At 1st level, you are always treated as if you've selected dragons with your favored prey class feature, in addition to the currently selected creature type.

At 5th level, you begin to grow a set of scales as hard as steel. Select 1 energy type (acid, cold, electricity, or fire); you gain resistance to that element equal to 1/2 your class level + your practitioner modifier (you can spend 8 hours of meditation to change this energy type). In addition, you gain a +2 natural armor bonus; this natural armor bonus increases by +1 at 10th, 15th, and 20th level.

As the scales slowly coalesce on your skin, your mind grows to despise vulnerability. Whenever you are not wearing armor or wielding a shield, you become shaken.

You may spend 1 spell point as a standard action to suppress this fear for 1 hour per reaper level.

At 9th level, you learn to channel your soul's majesty into a breath weapon which deals either acid, cold, electricity, or fire damage; you can spend 8 hours of meditation to change this energy type. Your breath weapon can be used as a 30 foot cone or 90 foot line, chosen each time you use it. Using this breath weapon is a standard action which costs 2 spell points, and it deals damage equal to 9d10 + your practitioner modifier, with a Reflex save for half damage (DC 10 + 1/2 class level + Practitioner modifier).

For each class level you possess past 9th, it deals an additional +1d10 damage. You can choose to reduce the damage die of this breath weapon to d6s instead of d10s; if you do, you can choose an additional damage type for it to deal; a creature must resist or be immune to both damage types or take full damage.

The act of diverting part of your soul into a breath weapon—the temporary weakening of your soul breeds contempt for your current body. Whenever you use draconic insufflation, you become fatigued for 1 round and suffer a -2 morale penalty to AC for 1 minute.

At 13th level, others begin to recognize your inner draconic majesty as you gain a fear aura as per the universal monster rules out to 30 feet, except that you calculate the save DC with your practitioner modifier.

Anyone who fails the save of this aura is frightened for a number of rounds equal to your practitioner modifier, while those who pass are instead shaken for the same duration. You may spend 1 spell point as a swift action to suppress or reactivate your fear aura.

Suppressing the might of your presence feels insulting and undignified, causing you to grow bitter and suffer a -5 penalty on all Charisma-based skill checks and ability checks as long as your fear aura is suppressed.

At 17th level, the terrible strength of your scaly soul is almost too much for your body to contain, and you may spend two spell points as a standard action to manifest this power as a translucent dragon's head, arms, and wings superimposed on your body for 1 minute. While projecting the wyrm spirit mantle, you gain the advanced template. You gain a +2 bonus on all rolls, including damage rolls and special ability DCs, a +4 bonus to AC and CMD, and +2 hit points per HD. Additionally, you gain a 60ft fly speed (good maneuverability) or a +60ft enhancement bonus to an exist fly speed if you already possess one.

Channeling the wyrm spirit mantle is dangerous for your body, as the excess power strains your normal bodily functions past their limits. At the end of the mantle's duration, you may spend 1 additional spell point as a free action to maintain the mantle for another minute. If you allow the mantle to end and fade away, you become exhausted and take 1 point of damage per reaper level per minute of maintaining the mantle.

At 20th level, if you surrender your soul, you gain the half dragon template. Your current natural armor stacks with the natural armor provided by this template, and rather than gaining a breath weapon, the damage of your draconic insufflation increases to 20d12 + two times your practitioner modifier (in the case of games that go past 20th level, for each additional class level you possess, your breath weapon deals an additional +1d12 damage).
At 2nd level, a reaper adds half their level to Survival skill checks made to follow tracks.

At 2nd level and every 2 levels afterwards, a reaper selects a reaper technique and learns new tactics for aiding in their hunt. Each reaper technique can only be selected once unless otherwise noted. The reaper chooses from the list below:

- **Accelerated Corruption: [Lost Champions Reaper: Apocrypha]** You gain your choice of either Transformation, Transformation, Hybrid, or Transformation, Improved as a bonus feat. You must meet the prerequisites of the chosen feat. You may select this reaper technique more than once, each time gaining an additional feat of your choice.
- **Armored Stride:** You may move in medium armor without a penalty to your movement speed. At 8th level, you may move in heavy armor without a penalty to your movement speed.
- **Bane of the Transformed: [Baron’s Otherworldly Citadel]** Choose up to three acquired templates. You always treat creatures with these templates as your favored prey. You may select this technique multiple times, each time selecting a different set of templates.
- **Champion:** Gain a Champion feat of your choice as a bonus feat. You must meet the prerequisites of the feat. You may select this reaper technique more than once. Each time it is selected, gain an additional feat.
- **Court Hunter (requires Partisan): [Baron’s Otherworldly Citadel]** Whenever you would select a favored prey with your reaper trophy, you may instead select a country with whose courtly graces you are wholly versed and studied. You apply your favored prey bonus against courtiers, officials, nobles, and gentry from that nation.
- **Deceptive Weapon:** Choose one weapon or shield with which you are proficient. You may add one other weapon to the chosen item. Each weapon acts as a mode for the deceptive weapon, being wielded and dealing damage as that weapon. Modes may be switched between as a free action. The deceptive weapon requires as many hands to wield as the current configuration. A deceptive weapon uses the same rules as a technician's invention for the purpose of rebuilding it, but does not count against the total number of inventions you can possess if you possess the invention class feature.
- **Deceptive Weapon, Improved (requires deceptive weapon): [Lost Champions Reaper: Apocrypha]** You may add 1 improvement from the technician's improved crossbow, improved gun, or improved melee weapon lists to 1 mode of a deceptive weapon you own that does not already have a technician improvement. You may select this reaper technique a second time, if you do, you instead add 1 improvement to both modes of your deceptive weapon.
- **Effigy of Hate:** You may craft a reaper trophy specific to an individual creature you have encountered, fueling its magic with your enmity towards it. As long as you hold this trophy, the individual your trophy represents is treated as your favoured prey. You may only own a number of trophies this way at once equal to your practitioner modifier.
- **Expanded Arsenal:** Gain a single talent of your choice from the Equipment sphere. You may select this reaper technique more than once. Each time it is selected, gain another equipment talent.
- **Expert Breaker: [Baron’s Otherworldly Citadel]** You may apply your favored prey bonus to any damage rolls you make against objects.
- **Familiar:** You gain a familiar as the wizard class feature, using your reaper level as your wizard level for this purpose.
- **Grim Harvester:** You gain Harvest Parts as a bonus feat. You may select technique this a second time to gain Grisly Ornament as a bonus feat.
- **Lord of Beasts (requires Cult of the Chimera or Cult of the Wolf): [Baron’s Otherworldly Citadel]** You always treat animals and vermin as your favored prey.
- **Manipulative Foe: [Lost Champions Reaper: Apocrypha]** You may add your favored prey bonus to Diplomacy and Intimidate checks against your favored prey.
- **Masked Stalker: [Lost Champions Reaper: Apocrypha]** You gain the dual identity class feature, treating your reaper level as your vigilante level. These levels stack with vigilante levels to determine your effective vigilante level.
- **Mutable Reality (requires fey hunter): [Lost Champions Reaper: Apocrypha]** Gain a surreal feat. You must meet the prerequisites of the feat. You may select this reaper technique more than once, each time gaining an additional surreal feat.
- **Necrotic Decay (requires undead hunter): [Lost Champions Reaper: Apocrypha]** Gain a necrosis feat. You must meet the prerequisites of the feat. You may select this reaper technique more than once, each time gaining an additional necrosis feat.
- **Nemesis of the Infinite (requires a cult which grants favored prey (outsider)): [Baron’s Otherworldly Citadel]** Choose a subtype. You always treat outsiders with that specific subtype as your favored prey, but treat any specific weaknesses from your cult as also applying to creatures and effects of that subtype (for example, if you have the Nether Brand class feature and choose chaotic, you become sickened for 1 minute whenever you touch or are damaged by a good- or lawful-aligned object or weapon. If you have the Hellraiser class feature, the saving throw penalty increases to -4 when the user is an outsider with the evil or chaotic subtype). You may select this technique multiple times, each time selecting a different subtype.
- **Obsessive Researcher:** You gain ranks in the Linguistics skill equal to your total Hit Dice; whenever you gain a Hit Die (such as when you gain a level) you gain an additional rank. If you already have ranks in the Linguistics skill you may immediately retrain them.
- **Occult Techniques:** You gain Psychic Sensitivity (Occult Adventures) as a bonus feat.
- **Purge Misconstruction (requires Mythos Hunter): [Baron’s Otherworldly Citadel]** By spending a spell point as a swift action, the mythos hunter may call out a creature from their literary tradition as being a misconstruction of the tradition’s original version. If the GM agrees that the creature is a misconstruction, the mythos hunter rolls doubles the damage bonus from favored prey against that target for a number of rounds equal to their reaper level. Examples of misconstruction include misapplication of traditional names (flesh golems), a profound misunderstanding of how the original entity functioned (druids with restrictions on using metal), or the use of a literary term or title for a completely unrelated creature (anything involving rakshasas).
- **Reaper’s Intuition: [Baron’s Otherworldly Citadel]** Whenever you perceive a favored prey that is disguised or has not made its otherworldly essence known, you gain an automatic check to identify the creature as your favored prey. To make this check, roll a 1d20 and add your reaper level and casting ability modifier (DC 10 + 1/2 the target’s Hit Dice + the target’s Cha modifier). A successful check means that you recognize the creature as one of your favored prey (though you do not necessarily know which type). You do not gain the bonus on weapon attacks and damage rolls against the creature if you do not recognize it as your favored prey.
- **Reprogram Foe: [Baron’s Otherworldly Citadel]** You can improve the initial attitude of a mindless creature that is your favored prey. This ability functions as wild empathy, except only against mindless creatures. You can use this ability on creatures with an Intelligence score of 1 or 2, but you take a –4 penalty on the check.
- **Seamless Guise (requires masked stalker): [Lost Champions Reaper: Apocrypha]** You gain a +20 circumstancebonus to Disguise checks to appear as your current identity, and not as your other identity.
- **Skilled Magic:** You gain one of the following feats: Cantrips, Circle Casting, Contingency, Counterspell, Improved Counterspell, Greater Counterspell, Ritual Caster. You must meet the prerequisites of the feat. You may select this reaper technique more than once. Each time it is selected, gain an additional feat.
- **Stance Dancer:** Gain a single talent of your choice with the [stance] tag that you qualify for. You cannot select this reaper technique if you do not qualify for any [stance] talents. You may select this reaper technique more than once. Each time it is selected, gain another [stance] talent.
- **Technological Paranoia (Requires Machine Cultist): [Baron’s Otherworldly Citadel]** You treat any creature wielding technological equipment or gizmos as constructs for the purpose of your favored prey.
- **Tricky:** Gain a rogue talent of your choice, treating your reaper level as your rogue level when determining the effects. This stacks with any rogue levels you possess. You may select this reaper technique more than once. Each time it is selected, gain another rogue talent.

At 3rd level, whenever a reaper uses a magical sphere effect which targets or includes in its effect only favored prey, the DCs and spell penetration checks for the effect each increase by 1. At 7th level and every 4 levels after, these bonuses increase by 1.

At 3rd level, a reaper always treats their weapons as being made of silver for the purposes of bypassing damage reduction. The blessing causes the reaper's held weapons to gleam as if cast in pale moonlight, though not so much as to impede attempts at stealth.

At 7th level, a reaper gains the scent universal monster ability. The range at which they can detect blood and bleeding creatures (including due to the bloodletter ability) is tripled, as if it were an overwhelming scent.

At 9th level, a reaper learns to sustain themselves with the minimum possible in order to hunt their prey relentlessly. The reaper only needs an eighth of their usual required food and water to survive, and the reaper only needs to sleep 2 hours per day to gain the benefit of 8 hours of sleep.

At 11th level, a reaper's gains intimate knowledge on how monsters act while trying to hide their true forms. The reaper adds half their level to all Perception checks to see through disguises, and ignores any magical bonuses to Disguise checks made to oppose their Perception checks.

At 13th level, a reaper's base scent range is doubled. This range increase is applied separately to multipliers for strong or overpowering scents, so the reaper could detect an overpowering scent like a bleeding creature as far as 180 feet away in still air.

At 17th level, a reaper has become so much like the monsters they study that reality itself has a difficult time telling if the reaper has joined their ranks or not. The reaper can pass as the creature type (or subtype) of the favored prey granted at 1st level by their cult class feature without the need for a Disguise check, and might be mistaken as one by a casual observer unless the reaper actively asserts their original identity.

Once the reaper reaches 20th level, this ability ceases to function and instead gives the reaper a +5 competence bonus to disguise checks.

At 19th level, a reaper's obsessive drive to hunt their favored prey has almost completely subsumed their mortality. The reaper no longer takes ability score penalties or receives ability score bonuses for aging and cannot be magically aged. As long as the reaper has attempted to hunt one of their favored prey within the last year, they cannot die of old age.

Additionally, the reaper no longer needs to sleep, eat, or drink in order to survive in a given day as long as they've drunk a mouthful of blood or inflicted bleed damage with their bloodletter ability that day.

At 20th level, a reaper faces a choice. Their occult studies have almost completely devoured their soul, and they must choose to reclaim or surrender their soul.

If the reaper surrenders their soul, they undergo a final transformation listed in the apotheosis ability of their chosen cult. If they instead reclaim their soul, the reaper reasserts their identity and purges the corruption their occult teachings have caused.

A reclaimed soul causes the reaper to lose all benefits of the cult class feature except for the permanent favored prey gained at 1st level. In exchange, the reaper immediately gains five combat feats of their choice, fast healing 5, and becomes immune to ability damage, ability drain, death effects, and level drain.

At 5th level, the flagellant learns to evade harm and solidify their body against assault, these defensive instincts facilitating an uneasy anxiety over broken equilibrium. The flagellant’s base Reflex save bonus from reaper levels is equal to 2 + 1/2 their reaper level. In addition, the flagellant gains a +2 natural armor bonus; this natural armor bonus increases by +1 at 10th level and every 5 levels thereafter. Whenever the flagellant is hit with an attack, they take a -2 penalty to attack rolls and AC and cannot benefit from morale bonuses for 1 round. The flagellant may spend a spell point as a free action to end these penalties.

If the flagellant succeeds at a Fortitude, Reflex, or Will saving throw against an attack that has a reduced effect on a successful save, they instead avoid the effect entirely. A helpless flagellant does not gain the benefit of this ability. This counts as having the evasion and stalwart class features. Whenever the flagellant fails a saving throw, they take a -2 penalty to saving throws and the saving throw DCs of their abilities and cannot benefit from insight bonuses for 1 round. The flagellant may spend a spell point as a free action to end these penalties.

Whenever the flagellant misses with an attack, the flagellant cannot be a willing target of any effect and must attempt saving throws to resist all abilities, even those cast by allies, for 1 round. The flagellant may spend a spell point to end this unwillingness as a free action.

At 17th level, the flagellant begins to detach themselves from existence and reason in order to find refuge. The flagellant becomes immune to pain effects and nonlethal damage as well as the stunned and dazed conditions. The flagellant takes a -10 penalty on all Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma-based skill checks, but may suppress this penalty for 1 minute by spending a spell point as a free action.

At 20th level, the flagellant learns to completely seal themselves off from reality and find a strange, distorted peace in their own mind. The flagellant becomes immune to mind-affecting effects, gains DR 10/-, and gains resistance 30 to all energy types. This replaces soul crisis.

At 6th level and every four levels thereafter, the bonus to saving throws increases by +1.
  * **Standard of the Swift Steed:** An ally who benefits from this banner increases a movement speed of their choice by 5 feet and gains a +1 bonus to attack rolls made as part of a charge. Additionally, allies who begin a charge while benefiting from this standard do not take a penalty to their AC. At 6th level and every four levels thereafter, the bonus to speed increases by 5 feet. An ally who begins their turn in this banner’s radius retains the benefits of this banner until the end of their turn, even if they move outside the banner’s area of effect.

A hunt master can select a new banner to fly by redesigning their existing banner over an 8 hour period. This replaces the reaper techniques gained at 2nd and 12th level.

At 9th, 13th, and 17th level, the machine cultist may select an additional invention in this manner.

At 17th level, a machine cultist uses the construct creature type for their reality shudders class feature.

This ability modifies reality shudders.

At 20th level, a machine cultist has completed their journey to become a perfect cyborg of living metal. The machine cultist's type changes to construct, except that they retain their Constitution score, do not receive bonus hit points for their size, retain their ability to heal damage on their own, are not immediately destroyed at 0 hit points, can be raised or resurrected normally, and are affected by magical healing effects normally. The machine cultist does not recalculate hit dice, base attack bonus, or saving throws.

This ability replaces soul crisis.

At 1st level, a magekiller may always treat any creature capable of casting spells or using magical sphere effects as their favoured prey.

This replaces the cult and reality shudders class features.
This replaces the cult and reality shudders class features.

At 5th level, a magekiller gains Counterspell as a bonus feat, even if they do not meet their prerequisites. If the magekiller already possess this feat, they may instead select and gain a different feat they meet the prerequisites for.

At 9th level, a magekiller gains Counterspell Mastery as a bonus feat, even if they do not meet their prerequisites. If the magekiller already possesses any of these feats, they may instead select and gain a different feat or feats they meet the prerequisites for.

At 13th level, whenever a magekiller successfully dispels a magic effect, suppresses a magical item, or counters a spell or magical effect with the Counterspell feat, they are refunded 1 spell point. The magekiller can only gain 1 spell point per use of the Counterspell feat, even if more than one spell, magical effect, or magic item is affected (such as with the Improved Counterspell feat).

At 17th level, whenever a magekiller successfully counters a spell with the Counterspell feat, they may cause harmful backlash towards the caster as a free action than can be taken even if it is not the magekiller's turn. The caster takes damage equal to 1d6 times the caster level of the countered ability, or half this damage with a successful Reflex save (DC = 10 + 1/2 the magekiller's HD + the magekiller's practitioner modifier).

At 20th level, a magekiller gains a +5 insight bonus to all saves against spells and magical sphere effects. Additionally, the magekiller does not need to spend an extra spell point to use the Counterspell Mastery feat.

This ability replaces soul crisis.

At 1st level, the mythos hunter receives the Scout sphere as a bonus sphere and Target Spotting as a bonus feat.

This replaces bloodletter

At 1st level, the mythos hunter selects a specific literary tradition in which creatures appear. Creatures sourced from the chosen tradition are considered to be the mythos hunter’s favored prey.

A literary tradition may take the form of a shared mythological tradition (such as Greek Mythology or Norse Poetry), the works of a specific author or group (such as Lewis Carroll or H.P. Lovecraft’s mythos cycle), or another grouping of works (such as “Wuxia” or “1970s Action Movies”). Creatures that the players and GM can agree are derived from a literary tradition also count as being part of that literary tradition (for example, halflings and treants could reasonably be considered part of a “Works of J.R.R. Tolkien” literary tradition). As humans tend to appear in the vast majority of stories, humans do not innately count as being part of any particular literary tradition.

In addition to creatures, characters who possess certain classes, feats, talents, or other features may also be treated as being part of a literary tradition for the purpose of favored mythos. For example, a Japanese Mythology literary tradition might include characters with levels in ninja while a Cyberpunk literary tradition might include characters with the Technomancy sphere. What ultimately qualifies as being part of a specific literary tradition is up to GM discretion.

This replaces the cult and reality shudders class features.
This replaces the cult and reality shudders class features.

A mythos hunter may select bardic masterpieces in place of reaper talents, using their mythos hunter level as their effective bard level. By spending a spell point as a free action, a mythos hunter may gain one round of bardic performance which lasts for 1 minute and can only be used for bardic masterpieces. At 4th level and every 4 levels thereafter, the number of bardic performance rounds gained from spending a spell point increases by 1.

At 5th level, the mythos hunter becomes extremely adept at spotting allusions and motifs in their surroundings, nuances which are often lost on their fellows. The mythos hunter gains the bardic knowledge and lore master abilities of a bard of their reaper level. Whenever the mythos hunter takes 10 or 20 on a Knowledge check using lore master, the mythos hunter takes a -4 penalty on non-Knowledge skill checks for 1 minute.

At 7th level, the mythos hunter gains Target Weakness as a bonus talent. When using Target Weakness, the effects of the talent last for a number of attacks equal to the mythos hunter’s practitioner modifier (minimum 2) rather than just the next attack.

At 13th level, the mythos hunter does not need to spend martial focus to use Target Weakness as a free action.

This replaces blood hunter and engorged scent

At 9th level, the mythos hunter may weave a story’s resonant power to replicate a storied success. When the mythos hunter attempts an attack roll, saving throw, or skill check, they may spend a spell point to roll twice and take the higher result. Whenever the mythos hunter uses this ability, they roll twice and take the lower result on all other d20 rolls until the end of their next turn.

At 13th level, a mythos hunter can spend a spell point as a swift action to invoke a primordial storytelling language that legendary creatures seem to innately understand. For a number of minutes equal to the mythos hunter’s level, they may communicate with their favored prey regardless of language (as the Logos sense from the Divination sphere with two spell points spent) and may apply their favored enemy bonus on all skill checks made against their favored prey (rather than just Bluff, Knowledge, Perception, Sense Motive, and Survival checks). When this effect ends, the mythos hunter is abruptly pulled back into their uncertain reality, becoming shaken for 1 hour.

At 17th level, a mythos hunter can offer themself up to the power of stories in order to send a chain of impossible phenomena resonating through their surroundings. Once per day, the mythos hunter can request a minor miracle. This request must be in line with the options for miracle that don’t cost powdered diamond. As usual for a miracle, the deity or other being the mythos hunter draws power from can choose whether or not to grant the request at its whim. Whenever the mythos hunter uses this ability, they suffer 1d6 points of ability burn to all of their ability scores.

At 20th level, a mythos hunter understands existence as an endless stream of connections, identifying how themes and elements depicted in any tale have-for better or worse-touched any given moment of the mythos hunter’s present experience. The mythos hunter treats all creatures as if the mythos hunter had scouted them and becomes immune to ability damage, ability drain, death effects, and level drain.

This replaces soul crisis

When a partisan would select a creature type for their favored prey, they must instead select a specific organization, such as a particular thieves’ guild. The partisan’s bonuses from favored prey apply against official members of this organization regardless of their creature type, but not against the organization’s allies, paid mercenaries, or forced labor. This ability only applies if the partisan knows that the target is a member of the organization. The reaper may change their favored prey by meditating on a faction trophy they've created for 1 minute. The partisan may still meditate on reaper trophies gained from other class features such as effigy of hate, gaining their effects as normal.

This ability alters favored prey.

The partisan may create a small object called a faction trophy with an object that has a symbol or written title associated with a specific organization and 1 hour of work. Whenever a partisan meditates on a faction trophy they've created, their favored prey type changes to the organization corresponding to the object used to make the trophy. These totems are otherwise treated as reaper trophies.

This ability replaces reaper totem.

At 1st level, a partisan gains the Gladiator sphere as a bonus talent, or a talent from the Gladiator sphere if they already possess the base sphere.

This ability replaces bloodletter.

Whenever a partisan would gain a reaper technique, they may choose to gain a social talent instead, treating their reaper level as their vigilante level. These levels stack with vigilante levels to determine the partisan's effective vigilante level. The partisan is always considered to be in their social identity, unless they have the ability to change into a vigilante identity from
another class feature.

This ability alters reaper techniques.

At 2nd level, a partisan chooses an eliciter emotion, gaining the minor power associated with that emotion and treating their partisan level as their eliciter level. At 5th level and every 3 levels thereafter, the partisan may choose to gain the minor power of a new emotion, or gain access to the next level of an emotion they already possess (lesser, greater, and master). A partisan cannot gain a lesser power before 8th level, a greater power before 14th level, or a master power before 20th level. All emotions are mind-affecting effects. If an emotion calls for a saving throw, the DC is equal to 10 + 1/2 their effective eliciter level + their casting ability modifier.

This ability replaces cult, blood hunter, engorged scent, discern true form, and reality shudders.
This ability replaces cult, blood hunter, engorged scent, discern true form, and reality shudders.

At 3rd level, a partisan may add their favored prey bonus to Disguise checks to appear to be a member of the organization chosen with their organized prey ability (this does not apply on Disguise checks to change their appearance and replace a specific member, but rather to checks related to appear to be a general member of the organization).

A partisan posing as a member of one of their organizations chosen with organized prey automatically defeats truth-telling magic (as if under the effects of glibness), but only for the purpose of claiming to be a member of the organization. Truth-telling magic can still expose them with a more indirect question, such as a member of a non-religious evil organization asking the partisan for the identity of their patron deity.

This ability replaces blessing of silver.
This ability replaces blessing of silver.

At 20th level, a partisan can make a special attack action against a favored prey, expending their martial focus. If the attack hits, the target takes damage normally and must succeed on a Will save (DC 10 + 1/2 their partisan level + their casting ability modifier) or become devoted to the partisan for 1 hour, gaining a disposition of helpful and obeying any orders the partisan gives to the exclusion of all other activities except those necessary for survival (eating, sleeping, etc.). The target never obeys obviously self destructive commands, and is allowed a new save with a +2 bonus to throw off the compulsion if asked to do something against its nature. A DC 25 Sense Motive check reveals the target is under compulsion.

The partisan may only have one target dominated in this fashion at a time; if the partisan successfully uses this ability to dominate a second target, the first is immediately released from service.

This ability replaces soul crisis.
